title: Gamaliel's advice (Acts 5:34–39)
hookLine: if it's of men it will fail, if of God you can't stop it
last: THE BIBLE KEEPS THE HARD STORIES.

lines: A MAN ASKS FOR THE ROOM.
cards: Voices are rising in a meeting. Someone is ready to fire someone. Then an older colleague raises a hand: wait.
Let's not decide this today. Give it six months and see. The apostles have been arrested again, and again they've kept preaching.
Back before the council, Peter says, we ought to obey God, rather than men. The council is furious; Luke says some of them want to kill the apostles. Then a man stands up and asks for the room.

teach.b: Luke introduces him with respect: a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law, honored by all the people. Later in Acts, Paul says he was brought up at the feet of Gamaliel.

And the Mishnah, the great early collection of Jewish teaching, says that when Rabban Gamaliel the Elder died, the glory of the Torah ceased. He has the apostles taken outside and speaks to his colleagues.

teach.h: THEUDAS AND JUDAS: CAME TO NOTHING.
teach.b: He reminds them of a Theudas who gathered about four hundred followers, and a Judas of Galilee who stirred people up in the days of the census. Both were killed; their movements scattered and came to nothing.

Then, in the Douay-Rheims: "for if this council or this work be of men, it will come to nought; But if it be of God, you cannot overthrow it, lest perhaps you be found even to fight against God." The council listens.

Instead of a death sentence, the apostles are beaten, ordered again not to speak in Jesus's name, and released. And Luke says they leave rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer for the name.
Gamaliel isn't a follower of Jesus here.

teach.h: LET TIME SHOW WHAT IT IS.
teach.b: He's a careful, devout teacher of his own tradition giving honest advice: don't force it; let God and time show what this is.
Christians have often reached for his test when something new appears in the Church: a movement, an order, an idea.
Some religious communities that began under suspicion, or were even disbanded for a time, were later recognized because they lasted and bore fruit.

how: The Church often waits years before approving a new religious community or a claimed private revelation, testing it over time by its fruits and its fidelity.

o: send the apostles out of Jerusalem quietly
if it's from God, you can't stop it, so wait
punish the apostles to end the movement

s: Gamaliel argued for executing the apostles
he urged the council to leave them alone and let God show.
Paul later says he studied under Gamaliel
Acts 22:3: brought up at the feet of Gamaliel.
the apostles left the council discouraged
they left rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer for the name.

games.q: you're on the council. the apostles keep preaching after you've forbidden it, and some want them dead. what does Gamaliel advise?
o: leave them alone; if it's of God you can't stop it.
games.why: if it be of men, it will come to nought; but if it be of God, you cannot overthrow it, lest you be found to fight against God.

practice: Think of something you're in a hurry to judge: a new person at work, a change at church or in your family, a plan someone else is excited about.

Notice the urge to settle it now, then picture setting it on a shelf with a date on it, three months away. If you pray, hold Gamaliel's words, if it be of God, and leave the outcome there; if you don't, just let it wait.

wordCard.voice: Gamaliel's advice. A respected Pharisee tells the council to leave the apostles alone: if this is of God, you can't stop it. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: fighters against God (Acts 5:39), the danger Gamaliel warns of.

carryVoice: Your line: if it be of god. Time has a way of showing what lasts. See you tomorrow.
